questions.question: An engine is 25% efficient and burns fuel releasing 3.6×10^6 J each cycle. How much work output per cycle results?
A 0.20 kg aluminum block at 200°C is placed in 0.50 kg of water at 20°C in an insulated container. Approximate final temperature? (c_Al ≈ 900 J/kg·°C, c_water ≈ 4200 J/kg·°C)
questions.explanation: Energy lost by Al = gained by water: 0.2·900(200−Tf) = 0.5·4200(Tf−20). Solving gives Tf ≈ 34°C.
steps: Set m c ΔT for both materials
questions.fastStrategy: Al has low heat capacity and small mass; water dominates, landing near room temp (~34°C).

questions.question: For an ideal gas at constant temperature, halving the volume will do what to the pressure?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P ∝ 1/V at fixed T, so halving V doubles P.
questions.fastStrategy: Inverse relationship: half the volume → double the pressure.

questions.question: A heat pump delivers 8000 kJ of heat to a house each hour while using 2500 kJ of electrical work. What is its heating COP?
steps: Divide delivered heat by work input
questions.fastStrategy: 8000 is a bit over triple 2500 → COP ≈ 3.2.

questions.question: Thermal conduction rate follows Q/t = k A ΔT / L. If both the area and length of a metal bar are doubled (ΔT and k unchanged), what happens to the conduction rate?
questions.explanation: Doubling area multiplies rate by 2, but doubling length divides by 2; effects cancel.
questions.fastStrategy: Area up ×2 and length up ×2 offset each other.

questions.question: An isothermal compression takes a gas from 0.040 m³ at 150 kPa to half the volume. What is the magnitude of the work done on the gas?
questions.explanation: For isothermal ideal gas, W = P1V1 ln(V2/V1). Here P1V1 = 150 kPa × 0.040 m³ = 6000 J. ln(0.5) ≈ −0.693. Work by gas = −4158 J, so work on gas is +4.2 kJ.
questions.fastStrategy: 6000 J × 0.693 ≈ 4.2 kJ (sign flips because it's compressed).

questions.question: How much energy melts 0.080 kg of ice at 0°C and warms the meltwater to 30°C? (Lf ≈ 334 kJ/kg, c_water ≈ 4200 J/kg·°C)
questions.explanation: Melt: Q1 = m Lf = 0.08×334 kJ ≈ 26.7 kJ. Warm water: Q2 = m c ΔT = 0.08×4200×30 ≈ 10.1 kJ. Total ≈ 36.8 kJ ≈ 37 kJ.
questions.fastStrategy: About 27 kJ to melt plus 10 kJ to warm → roughly 37 kJ.

questions.question: If a perfect blackbody's absolute temperature doubles, its radiated power (per area) changes by what factor?
questions.explanation: Stefan–Boltzmann law: P/A ∝ T^4. Doubling T gives 2^4 = 16 times the power.

questions.question: A refrigerator removes 500 J from the cold space and exhausts 650 J to the room each cycle. How much work input does the compressor use?
questions.explanation: Energy balance: W_in = Q_hot − Q_cold = 650 − 500 = 150 J.
steps: Apply first law to the cycle
Subtract cold removal from heat exhaust
questions.fastStrategy: Hot out minus cold in gives the required work.

questions.question: Air rising near a warm radiator and sinking as it cools is primarily an example of:
questions.explanation: Bulk motion of fluid due to heating differences is convection; conduction is molecule-to-molecule, radiation is EM emission.
steps: Other modes do not move bulk air
questions.fastStrategy: Moving warm air = convection (not conduction or radiation).
